summary: H.R. 9959, the Green New Deal for Public Schools Act, establishes federal grant programs within the Department of Education, Department of Energy, and other agencies to fund environmental upgrades, facility retrofits, educational equity planning, and climate resiliency projects in public elementary and secondary schools, Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) schools, and schools funded by the BIE.

affected_groups.effect: Receive grant funding, technical assistance, and loans to upgrade facilities, hire additional staff, build zero-carbon schools, and implement climate resiliency and equity plans.
affected_groups.group: Public and BIE Schools and Local Educational Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Gain opportunities for full-time employment positions, salary increases, training, professional development, and inclusion in collective bargaining units.
affected_groups.group: Educators, Paraprofessionals, and School Support Staff

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from mandatory funding increases under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) and accessibility improvements in school facilities.
Subject to prevailing wage (Davis-Bacon Act), Buy American requirements, apprenticeship utilization targets, and localized hiring preferences for funded construction and retrofit projects.

key_provisions: Establishes an Office of Sustainable Schools within the Department of Education to coordinate resource block grants and educational equity grants with climate capital facilities and climate resiliency programs.
Provides $446,000,000,000 over 10 years for climate capital facilities grants administered by the Secretary of Energy to conduct healthy green retrofits and construct new healthy zero-carbon schools.

Provides $250,000,000,000 over 10 years for resource block grants to qualified local educational agencies to hire eligible educators and support staff, increase paraprofessional pay, and establish community partnerships.
Provides $100,000,000 for educational equity planning and implementation grants to eliminate intra-region education inequities across regional consortia of local educational agencies.
Amends the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) to provide mandatory annual funding levels scaling from fiscal year 2027 through 2036 and subsequent years.
Appropriates $74,000,000,000 annually for 10 years to carry out part A of title I of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965.

Establishes a Climate Change Resiliency Program providing $4,000,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2037 to help public and BIE schools serve as community resiliency centers during disasters.
missing_information: The total combined fiscal impact across all provisions beyond the explicitly stated appropriations has not been fully tabulated in the text.
Specific administrative rules and exact application timelines aside from statutory introductory windows are left to the discretion of the respective agency secretaries.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9959, the Green New Deal for Public Schools Act, establishes federal grant programs within the Department of Education, Department of Energy, and other agencies to fund environmental upgrades, facility retrofits, educational equity planning, and climate resiliency projects in public elementary and secondary schools, Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) schools, and schools funded by the BIE.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates sweeping, multi-billion-dollar federal investments spanning a ten-year period aimed at overhauling public school infrastructure, expanding staffing and mental health services, altering energy consumption and climate resilience standards in educational facilities nationwide, and revising federal education funding formulas.
